title: Testing, Creativity and the Grand Finale
subtitle: You Are Now a Game Creator!

scenes.name: Lesson opener
scenes.visual: Lesson card: 'LESSON 6 · FINALE', with a gold star tile.
scenes.onScreen: LESSON 6 · You Are Now a Game Creator!

scenes.name: Save and run
scenes.visual: IDE with all three files in the sidebar. The cursor clicks Save (check flash) and then Run, and the preview loads the finished game.
scenes.transition: The preview expands to near full frame.

lines.text: Welcome to our final lesson, creators!
Here are our three files, all finished. Before we share our game, we have one more important job: testing.
Developers save and test their work often. Save... and Run.

scenes.name: Tester's checklist
scenes.visual: Game large on the left; a TESTER'S CHECKLIST on the right whose items tick green as each is proven: Cards flip ✓, Matching pair stays ✓, Wrong pair flips back ✓, Moves counter ✓, Timer ✓, Celebration screen ✓, Play again ✓, Difficulty ✓. Gameplay is driven by the same simulator as Lessons 1 and 5, so the numbers on screen are consistent.
scenes.camera: Push in on the stat being checked.
scenes.sfx: Game sounds, a tick per checklist item.

lines.text: Let's play our game like a tester, and check every part.
First, we select two cards. Do they flip? Yes!
Now let's find a matching pair. They turn green, and stay face up. Perfect.
Now two cards that don't match. They show for a moment, then turn back over. Correct!
Is the moves counter right? Three turns, three moves. Yes!
Is the timer counting? Yes. It started with our very first click.
Let's finish the game... and there's the celebration screen.
Play again starts a fresh game. And if we change the difficulty to Easy, we get four pairs.
Everything works! Testing helps us find mistakes before other people do.

scenes.name: Debugging practice
scenes.visual: A separate, clearly labelled PRACTICE PROJECT in the IDE (the project name in the sidebar reads 'Debugging practice'). Its index.html has href="styles.css". Run: the preview shows the plain, unstyled page. A detective magnifier checks HTML ✓, CSS ✓, then the link line (red underline). The sidebar's 'style.css' and the code's 'styles.css' are shown together with the extra 's' circled. The cursor deletes the 's', then Save and Run: the styled page returns.
scenes.camera: Zoom between the link line and the sidebar.
scenes.onScreen: PRACTICE PROJECT · styles.css ≠ style.css · DEBUGGING = finding and fixing mistakes
scenes.sfx: Gentle 'uh-oh' on the broken run, magnifier ping, sparkle on the fix.

lines.text: But what happens when something goes wrong? Let's look at a practice project.
In this practice project, someone typed styles dot C S S, with an extra S.
lines.caption: In this practice project, someone typed styles.css, with an extra s.

lines.text: We click Run... and oh no! All our colours and cards have disappeared.
Let's investigate. The HTML looks fine. The CSS looks fine. So, the problem must be the link between them.
The file is called style dot C S S, but the link says styles dot C S S. The browser can't find a file with that name!
lines.caption: The file is called style.css, but the link says styles.css. The browser can't find a file with that name!

lines.text: Let's remove the extra S, save, and run again.
lines.caption: Let's remove the extra s, save, and run again.

lines.text: Fixed! Finding and fixing mistakes like this is called debugging. Every developer does it, every single day.

scenes.name: Creative challenges
scenes.visual: Seven numbered challenge cards (styled as Number Match cards, numerals 1–7) flip up one by one, each with a mini live example: page background changes colour; the heading text changes; Quicksand weights 300→700 shown; the select's pair number changes (max 8, because numberWords stops at Eight); cards grow and shrink; the card back turns another colour; letters A/B/C replace numbers on cards. Each card shows the file and the property to edit.
scenes.camera: Pan along the row; each card enlarges when it is described.
scenes.onScreen: 1 Background · 2 Heading · 3 Font weight · 4 Pairs · 5 Card size · 6 Card back · 7 Your own version

lines.text: Now it's your turn to make this game your own. Here are some challenges.
Challenge one: change the background colour of the page.
Challenge two: change the heading to something new.
Challenge three: try different Quicksand font weights, from three hundred to seven hundred.
lines.caption: Challenge three: try different Quicksand font weights, from 300 to 700.

lines.text: Challenge four: change the number of pairs in one of the levels. You can go up to eight.
Challenge five: make the cards bigger or smaller.
Challenge six: give the card backs a new colour.
And challenge seven: create your very own version of the game. Maybe with letters, colours, or shapes instead of numbers?
Don't worry about breaking things. You can always fix them. That's how we learn!

scenes.name: The finished project
scenes.visual: Cinematic montage, no narration: macro on a card flip; a matched pair turning green; the timer ticking; the progress bar filling; the IDE beside the preview with code lines highlighting as the matching game event happens (code ↔ result); the celebration screen. Flat parallax cards float across the deep-green frame between shots.
scenes.camera: Varied: macro push-ins, slow lateral moves, one 3D tilt.
scenes.music: Bed at full: the musical peak of the series.

scenes.name: Celebrate the learner
scenes.visual: A journey line draws across the frame with milestones: an empty HTML file → structure boxes → the styled card → a flipping card → the finished game. On 'very own memory matching game' a big 'I MADE THIS!' stamp lands. The final lines run over the Paisley Studio badge, then the tagline types: 'Imagine it. Build it. Make it yours.' Final branded frame.
scenes.camera: Lateral track along the journey line, then locked on the logo.
scenes.onScreen: I MADE THIS! · PAISLEY STUDIO · Imagine it. Build it. Make it yours.
scenes.sfx: Milestone pops, stamp thump (soft), closing audio signature.
scenes.music: Bed resolves to the final chord.
scenes.transition: Hold on the logo, fade to black.

lines.text: Take a moment, and look at what you have achieved.
You started with an empty HTML document.
You learned how to structure a webpage, style it with CSS, and bring it to life using JavaScript.
And now, you have built your very own memory matching game!
Remember, every great developer started by learning one small thing at a time.
Keep experimenting. Keep creating. And never stop being curious.
This is Paisley Studio.
Imagine it. Build it. Make it yours.
